title: Boundary Lab — verdict examples
notice: Fictional scenarios for education only. These are not real audit results and are not a report compatible with report-schema.json.

confirmed.label: CONFIRMED
confirmed.title: A boundary violation is observed.
rows: A user in tenant A must not be able to read documents belonging to tenant B.
In this fictional local test, an authenticated user from tenant A reads a dummy document owned by tenant B.
Verify the current user's tenant and the document's ownership before returning any data.
confirmed.note: A real finding must include the complete source path, validation conditions, and observed impact.

needs_validation.label: NEEDS VALIDATION
needs_validation.title: A critical fact is still unknown.
rows: Authentication is delegated to an external gateway, so the application alone does not show the full control.
The authentication policy applied to this route by the deployed gateway still needs to be verified.
Ask the owner to confirm the configuration, or reproduce the relevant policy in an isolated local environment.
needs_validation.note: Do not assign severity to an item awaiting validation. An unverified hypothesis is not a confirmed vulnerability.

rejected.label: REJECTED
rejected.title: An existing control blocks the path.
rows: A user-supplied file path appeared capable of escaping its permitted directory.
In this fictional example, the trusted input layer normalizes the path and rejects access outside the root before it reaches the file operation.
The actual input path is blocked by an effective control, so the candidate is rejected.
rejected.note: A missing additional defense is not itself a vulnerability when an existing control already prevents the attack.
